en: Agreement or harmony; a formal treaty; to give or grant
hook: ACCORD: hearts (cor) in agreement.
story: After months of talks, the two countries signed a peace accord. Everyone was in accord: the war must end. The hero was accorded a state funeral. Accord means agreement, a formal treaty, or to grant.

en: To stick firmly; to follow a rule or belief
hook: ADHERE: like ADHESIVE tape.
story: The stamp didn't adhere to the wet envelope. Nadia adheres strictly to her study schedule: two hours every morning, no exceptions. To adhere is to stick, or to follow faithfully. An adherent is a follower.

en: Created for a particular purpose only, not planned in advance
hook: AD HOC: Latin for 'for this' — for this one purpose only.
story: When the flood hit, the students formed an ad hoc relief committee within hours. It dissolved once the water receded. Ad hoc means arranged for a specific purpose, often improvised. Synonyms: impromptu, makeshift.

en: Including everything
hook: ALL-ENCOMPASSING: a COMPASS that circles everything.
story: Her grief after her mother's death was all-encompassing; it filled every hour, every room, every thought. The new law was all-encompassing, covering every type of business. All-encompassing means including everything. Synonym: comprehensive.

en: A short, wise statement of a general truth
hook: APHORISM: a short AFFIRMATION of truth.
story: Grandpa loved aphorisms: 'Slow and steady wins the race.' 'A stitch in time saves nine.' Each one packed a life lesson into a few words. An aphorism is a concise statement of wisdom. Synonyms: maxim, adage, proverb.

en: A standard against which things are measured
hook: BENCHMARK: a mark on the workbench to measure against.
story: A GRE score of 320 became Tanvir's benchmark; every practice test was measured against it. Benchmark means a standard of comparison. Companies use benchmarks to compare their performance with competitors.

en: Damaged or spoiled; suffering from decay
hook: BLIGHT: a plant disease that withers crops.
story: The once-thriving neighborhood became blighted after the factory closed: empty shops, broken windows, and garbage in the streets. A blight is a plant disease. Blighted means ruined or decayed. A career blighted by scandal.

en: Peacefully satisfied
hook: CON-TENT (stress on TENT): happy in your little tent.
story: The old fisherman didn't have much money, but he was content: a small house, a loving family, and the river at sunset. Content means peacefully satisfied. Contentment is a kind of happiness that doesn't need more.

en: Reduced in quality, value, or moral character
hook: DE-BASED: brought to a BASE (low) level.
story: Ancient rulers sometimes debased their coins, mixing cheap metal with silver. The debased coins lost value. Today, critics say political debate has been debased by insults and lies. Debased means lowered in quality or value.

en: Causing one to feel unsettled or uneasy
hook: DIS-CONCERT-ING: throws the CONCERT out of tune.
story: The interviewer's long silence after each answer was disconcerting; Rafi couldn't tell if she was impressed or disappointed. Disconcerting means unsettling. Synonyms: disturbing, unnerving, discomfiting.

en: Still in existence
hook: EXTANT: still standing, not EXTINCT.
story: Only three copies of the ancient manuscript are extant; all the others were lost in fires and floods. Extant means still existing. Its opposite is extinct. Many of Shakespeare's letters are no longer extant.

en: Natural ease or skill in doing something
hook: GRE trick: FACILITY means ease — she has a facility for languages.
story: Mitu has a remarkable facility for languages; she picked up Japanese in a year and Spanish in six months. On the GRE, facility means natural ease or aptitude, not a building.

en: Active or occurring in irregular bursts; not steady
hook: FITFUL: in FITS and starts.
story: Before the exam, Arif had a fitful night's sleep: waking every hour, tossing, turning, and checking the clock. Fitful means irregular and interrupted. Synonyms: sporadic, intermittent.

en: To encourage or stir up violent or unlawful behavior
hook: INCITE: light a fire INSIDE the crowd.
story: The speaker was arrested for inciting violence after urging the crowd to attack shops. To incite is to provoke or stir up trouble. Synonyms: foment, instigate, provoke.

en: To persuade; to bring about or cause
hook: INDUCE: lead (duce) INTO.
story: Nothing could induce Grandma to leave her village home for the city. The warm milk induced sleep within minutes. To induce is to persuade or to cause. Doctors can induce labor.

en: An inappropriate expression or action; unhappiness
hook: IN-FELICITY: NOT FELICITOUS, not well chosen.
story: The speech was strong, but marred by a few infelicities, like calling the grieving widow's husband 'the late great entertainer' at a solemn memorial. An infelicity is an awkward or inappropriate choice of words. It can also mean unhappiness.

en: Able to be understood
hook: INTELLIGIBLE: your INTELLIGENCE can grasp it.
story: The phone line was so bad that only half of what Nadia's father said was intelligible. The professor's handwriting was barely intelligible either. Intelligible means understandable. Its opposite is unintelligible.

en: Serving as a temporary substitute
hook: MAKESHIFT: MAKE do in a SHIFT.
story: After the cyclone, families lived in makeshift shelters of bamboo, plastic sheets, and tin. A makeshift hospital was set up in the school. Makeshift means temporary and improvised. Synonyms: ad hoc, stopgap.

en: Former
hook: ONETIME: ONE TIME in the past.
story: The onetime cricket star now runs a small coaching academy in his hometown. Onetime means former. Synonyms: erstwhile, previous, quondam.

en: Taking advantage of opportunities without regard to principles
hook: OPPORTUNISTIC: grabs every OPPORTUNITY, ethical or not.
story: During the flood, opportunistic traders doubled the price of drinking water. The opportunistic politician switched parties three times, always joining whoever was winning. Opportunistic means exploiting chances selfishly.

en: Seeming reasonable or probable
hook: PLAUSIBLE: deserves APPLAUSE for sounding right.
story: Arif's excuse for being late, a broken bus and a traffic jam, was plausible in Dhaka; the teacher believed him. Plausible means believable. But careful: a plausible story isn't always true. Specious arguments are plausible but false.

en: Behavior intended to impress or mislead
hook: POSTURING: striking a POSTURE (pose) for show.
story: Before the election, both parties engaged in posturing: loud promises, angry speeches, and dramatic walkouts. None of it changed any policy. Posturing is behavior meant to impress rather than achieve something.

en: Having great power or effect
hook: POTENT: full of POTENTIAL power.
story: The new medicine was so potent that a single dose cured the infection. Fear is a potent weapon in politics. Potent means powerful and effective. Synonyms: strong, forceful, efficacious.

en: No longer needed; unnecessary repetition
hook: REDUNDANT: RE-DONE, repeated without need.
story: 'Free gift' is redundant; all gifts are free. When the factory installed robots, many workers became redundant. Redundant means unnecessary, especially through repetition. In engineering, redundancy means backup systems.

en: Too important or sacred to be interfered with
hook: SACRO-SANCT: SACRED and SANCTIFIED.
story: For Mitu's family, Friday lunch together was sacrosanct; no job, exam, or friend could interrupt it. Sacrosanct means sacred and untouchable. Synonym: inviolable.

en: Showing sharp judgment, especially in practical matters
hook: SHREWD: sharp as a SHREW's teeth.
story: The shrewd shopkeeper noticed that students bought tea and samosas after exams, so he opened a stall right outside the exam hall. Shrewd means sharp and practically clever. Synonyms: astute, canny.

en: Plain; without decoration
hook: UN-ADORNED: not ADORNED.
story: The mosque's interior was unadorned: white walls, a simple carpet, and soft light. Its beauty came from its simplicity. Unadorned means plain and undecorated. Synonyms: austere, simple. Its opposite is ornate.

en: Serving as a farewell
hook: VALEDICTORY: say VALE (farewell).
story: In her valedictory speech, the retiring headmistress thanked every student, teacher, and cleaner, and the hall filled with tears. Valedictory means relating to farewell. A valedictorian gives the farewell speech at graduation.

en: Justified; having good reason
hook: WARRANTED: a WARRANT gives justification.
story: Given the cyclone warning, the decision to close the schools was fully warranted. Rafi's anger was unwarranted; nobody had insulted him. Warranted means justified. Unwarranted means without good reason.

en: Having a feeling of vague or regretful longing
hook: WISTFUL: WISHFUL with a little sadness.
story: Looking at old photos of his childhood village, now swallowed by the river, Grandpa had a wistful smile. Wistful means gently longing, often for the past. Synonyms: nostalgic, yearning, melancholy.
